S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in living condition (new home, remodeling, deterioration of neighborhood or home)
patient_info.stressor: Leyda’s concern became noticeable after she and her husband remodeled their bathroom, adding brighter lighting and a larger mirror as part of a practical home update. During her morning routine, she began dwelling on a slight perceived change in her skin and facial contours, then developed small but persistent checking and comparing habits before leaving for the courthouse. She remained reliable at work and active with family cooking, gardening, and book club, but the extra preparation time made her late to yoga and occasionally caused her to avoid casual photos at community events. She brought it up during a primary care visit while asking about cosmetic options, and her physician referred her for psychiatric assessment when it became clear the concern was causing functional strain.

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: I’m here because ever since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing that the skin around my cheeks and jaw looks uneven or kind of saggy to me, even though my husband says he can’t really see what I’m talking about.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Most mornings I end up checking my face from a few angles and putting on a little extra makeup before I leave for the courthouse, and sometimes I compare my face to women I see at work or avoid being in casual pictures if I’m not feeling okay about it.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I still get my work done, but the extra time I spend getting ready has made me rush into the courthouse a few mornings and miss the start of yoga more than once. I’ve also skipped a few casual photos at book club and community events because I didn’t want to worry about how my face would look.
